correctness.rationale: The known Gaussian localization identity makes H(Ω)=double integral over Ω of exp(-pi|z-w|^2). Converting to squared-radius coordinates yields smooth upper-limit integrals. Expanding the two radial upper limits yields cross-boundary Gaussian circle convolution e^-2A I_|n|(2A), and self-boundary term -e^-2A I1(2A) after radial differentiation of the disk potential via divergence theorem. The n=0 constraint is removed by exact area conservation; n=1 cancels as translations. Bessel ratio derivative r_k′=1-(2k+1)r_k/x-r_k^2 plus r_k<1 initially proves strict I_{k+1}<I_k for k>=1; n=2 thus uniquely minimizes positive curvature. Standard Bessel asymptotics yield c(A)=A+O(A^2), c(A)~3/(8 sqrt(pi) A^(3/2)). Independent quadrature of the double Gaussian boundary energy for two areas and four angular modes confirms expansion, but each fixed u has only pointwise o(epsilon^2) remainder; not a uniform global stability proof.
